CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.isLimitAux'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y Z : C} {f : X ⟶ Z}
  {g : Y ⟶ Z} (t : PullbackCone f g)
  (create :
    (s : PullbackCone f g) →
      { l //
        l ≫ t.fst = s.fst ∧ l ≫ t.snd = s.snd ∧ ∀ {m : s.pt ⟶ t.pt}, m ≫ t.fst = s.fst → m ≫ t.snd = s.snd → m = l }) :
  IsLimit t
```
***
This is another convenient method to verify that a pullback cone is a limit cone. It
only asks for a proof of facts that carry any mathematical content, and allows access to the
same `s` for all parts.

  {g : Y ⟶ Z} {t : PullbackCone f g} (ht : IsLimit t) {W : C} (h : W ⟶ X) (k : W ⟶ Y) (w : h ≫ f = k ≫ g) :

Because this is in the `Eq` namespace, if you have a variable `h : a = b`,
`h.symm` can be used as shorthand for `Eq.symm h` as a proof of `b = a`.
